question.problem:
$$
f(y,z)=⟨\text{_____},\,y,\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(y,z)$ above parametrizes the elliptic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $5x=10{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.worked_solution:
Solving our equation for $x,$ we obtain

$$
5x=10{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}\,⟹\,x=2{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{5}{z}^{2}.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨2{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{5}{z}^{2},\,y,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $y\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $2{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{5}{z}^{2}.$
